What degraded

  • THE RUN HOLDS AND DOES NOT MERGE. scripts/site/ask_pack.py --self-test is red in the gates job at 40,894 characters against its 40,000 ceiling. Measured on origin/main the same check reads 39,826, and this run's admissions are a line of index each. The file is human lane with no rebuild_by, so neither of the two fixes it names is one this run may write.
  • The email's image URLs point at the run branch rather than main, because the deck is not on main.
  • Two of this run's six admissions were duplicates of decisions already in the record and were removed the same day. A review bot on the pull request found both. Nothing in this project compares an admission against the record it is being added to, and that gate is written up for the upgrade lane rather than built here.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Austin's parks camera order and the ordinance behind it, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

The rule arrived inside a parks item.

Austin City Council adopted Resolution No. 20260812-017 on August 12th, 2026. It directs the City Manager to buy and turn on parks security equipment. The same text bars that officer from considering a camera or drone that depends upon artificial intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis.

April had already said no. Artificial intelligence or machine learning tools are already among what is not permitted in City Code Chapter 2-19. That listing leaves an exception for whatever the city's own policy allows. The August clause leaves none. It also binds one officer for one kind of purchase.

The council's own action notes record the item approved and send the vote details to minutes approved at a later meeting. The resolution defines that dependence nowhere. Who decides whether a camera depends upon it?

#AustinCityCouncil #TRUSTAct #AustinParks

2. The first comment

The machine changed itself

  • `plan_render_check.acceptance_items` reads the WHOLE acceptance list. PyYAML is the primary route, the same parser `dossier_check` has always used on the same blocks, and a continuation-aware regex is the fallback for a block PyYAML refuses.
    The block was taken with `^acceptance:\s*\n((?: - .*\n)+)`, whose repetition ends at the first line that is not two spaces and a dash. That is the continuation of an item long enough to wrap, so THE BLOCK ENDED AT THE FIRST WRAPPED ITEM and everything after it in that slide's list was never read. The gate has been certifying a fraction of every plan since it was written, and it is the gate that exists because the plan-versus-render defect shipped in all three of this project's early runs.
  • `sources_block` prints its day count provenance line only when an aggregate carries `from_date` and `to_date` and the two differ, rather than when an aggregate is labelled `kind: duration` or `kind: span`.
    `kind` is a label a writer types, and every duration a source states in its own words is legitimately labelled `duration` too. So the sentence `Day counts computed in compute.py from the source dates above.` rode along on decks that performed no subtraction anywhere. That is a provenance claim, made to a reader, about a computation that did not happen, published by the one file whose own docstring says no count and no date in its output is typed there. GATE_LESSONS entry 41 ("A fact the code branches on, carried only in prose") is the rule this is a case of, one level up from a numeral: a fact the build BRANCHES ON needs a field, because a decision derived from a label is a decision derived from whatever wording somebody used that day.
  • `claims_check` sweeps every prose snapshot in the run's own `sources/` for the deck's subject nouns and warns on any provision that names one and holds no claim's quote and is named nowhere in `rejected` or `notes`.
    Deck no. 18's thesis was refuted by Section 2-19-9 of an ordinance the run had fetched in full, cited six other sections of, and never opened. The ordinance names artificial intelligence in twelve places across five provisions and the run had read one. A second one the same run, the same shape: the council's Actions Taken By Council page was linked from an agenda the run had already fetched, and the run's rejected list said the agenda publishes no vote, which was true of the page's prose and skipped the link sitting on it. Both were found by a scoring judge. THE WHOLE PIPELINE IS ORIENTED ONE WAY. claims_check, aggregate_check, numeral_trace, noun_trace, locator_trace and absence_check all ask whether what the deck PRINTS traces back to a source. Not one asked whether what a SOURCE says came forward. This runs at Phase 6, before a frame exists, which is the last moment the answer is cheap.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

THIS RUN HOLDS AND NEEDS YOU, AND ONE ACTION CLEARS IT. Raise MAX_INDEX_CHARS in scripts/site/ask_pack.py, or roll the decisions up the way the register, the reservoirs and the dossiers already are, then merge PR 272. Everything else is done and on the branch, and none of it is on main, because that one CI step is red and the file is not in this run's lane. scripts/site/ask_pack.py --self-test measures the always-sent ask index at 40,894 characters against a ceiling of 40,000. Measured on main the same check reads 39,826, which passes by 174. Today's admissions are a line each at roughly 222 characters, which accounts for the whole of it and nothing else moved. Removing two duplicate admissions took it from 41,381 to 40,894 and did not clear it. ownership.yaml gives scripts/site/ask_*.py to human with no rebuild_by, and both fixes the file itself names are edits to it. Roll the decisions up the way the register, the reservoirs and the dossiers already are, or raise MAX_INDEX_CHARS and accept the bill. The record was not trimmed to fit instead, because shedding 1,500 characters means cutting about 13 from each of 118 headlines and this project does not bend the record around a gate. Main was already 174 characters from the ceiling before today, so this was days away whatever this run did. THE RECORD. The worklist cleared in full, 97 due to 0 due. Six decisions admitted and two of them removed the same day as duplicates, two held for naming no Texas place, one re-sourced off capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs onto senate.texas.gov because the first disallows this agent. Two real quote corrections: tx-2026-0056-c3 had dropped the word also from a board's own sentence, and tx-2026-0122-c1 had spliced two passages separated by an attribution. The record stands at 116 items and the site is rebuilt byte for byte from it. THE DECK, AND THE THING WORTH YOUR TIME. Carousel no. 18's first thesis was FALSE and a scoring judge found it. The deck argued that Austin's April ordinance merely WEIGHED artificial intelligence as one of ten privacy assessment factors and that the August resolution turned it into a bar. Section 2-19-9 of that same ordinance, six pages past the section the run read, lists artificial intelligence or machine learning tools among the technologies that are NOT PERMITTED, except as consistent with City policy. The run had the whole fourteen page extraction in hand and had cited six other sections of it. Nothing was published. The spine was rebuilt on what the whole instrument says, which is that April prohibited the tools with a door in it and August closed the door and narrowed the room, and the deck is better for it. IT HAPPENED TWICE. A second judge found the council's own Actions Taken By Council page, linked from an agenda this run had fetched on its first pass and never opened. It records the item approved and publishes no tally, so the closing frame's absence was right and had not been earned. It has now. Twice in one run the answer was inside something already in hand, and both times a judge found it rather than a gate. THE RECORD ITEM WAS CORRECTED TOO. tx-2026-0129 said the December 9th date was a committee meeting a reader can attend. It is the date by which an update is owed. That is fixed on the published page along with the April prohibition, because the record is the deliverable that outlives the post. NOTHING PROMPTED. prompt_audit read the debug log for both processes and measured 1,891 tool calls, none of which waited on a permission decision. That is the reading that counts, rather than a run saying it noticed no prompt. TWO OF TODAY'S ADMISSIONS WERE DUPLICATES AND A REVIEW BOT FOUND BOTH, NOT A GATE. tx-2026-0130 was the same NSF operations center already in the record as tx-2026-0121, down to the identical verbatim quote and the same announcement URL. tx-2026-0126 was the same Senate Water committee sitting already in the record as tx-2026-0096, and its one new piece of evidence, the Senate video archive recording, is folded into that entry. Neither had reached main, so removing them rewrote nothing a reader had seen. Nothing in this project compares an admission against the record it is being added to. dedupe_check compares the DECK against recent decks. A duplicate inflates the count the front page prints and splits one decision's evidence across two pages, two feeds and two ask index lines. That is the run's worst record defect and it is written up for the upgrade lane. FOUR MORE REAL FINDINGS FROM THE SAME REVIEW. A report deadline was filed as a hearing, so the calendar offered readers a proceeding that does not exist, and this run had already corrected that same error in the item's prose and left it standing in the data. A first of the month was computed for a curriculum the university says starts in July 2026 with no day given. A status read pending on an investigation whose own summary says the record can't know its state. And a contextual date from 2025 was starting a 2026 investigation's timeline. All four are fixed.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
